title: Testing SubQ Savant 1.4 on my personal benchmark
subtitle: 14 minutes, 259 turns, $0.23 — fastest run on the board, stopped at S7.
description: A 7-slide visual breakdown of SubQ Savant 1.4 on OMP v19.0.1: 1.82s/turn inference speed, head-to-head with deepseek-v4-flash on OMP, why deferring S1 broke S7 Ctrl-C, S3 micro-turn churn, and field caveats.
seoDescription: 7-slide breakdown of SubQ Savant 1.4 on OMP v19.0.1: 1.82s/turn speed, deepseek-v4-flash comparison, why deferring S1 broke S7 Ctrl-C, and caveats.

slides.label: COVER
slides.headlinePrimary: Testing SubQ Savant 1.4 on my personal benchmark.
slides.lead: The **fastest run on the entire leaderboard** (`1.82s/turn` across `259` turns) cleared live HTTP & HTTPS, then surrendered on terminal `Ctrl-C`.

slides.label: SAME-HARNESS COMPARISON
slides.headlinePrimary: On the exact same OMP v19 setup.
slides.footnote: * Both scored 6/7 on OMP v19 (#high), failing S7 on different OTP signal bugs. DeepSeek ran Off-Peak ($0.25 Peak).

steps.title: Skipped S1's entry-point rule
steps.desc: Probed PTY `Ctrl-C`, saw BEAM's `BREAK` menu, yet kept `cb` as a bare escript and punted the fix to S7.

steps.title: 71 turns fighting the VM
steps.desc: Spent **$0.09** (`39%` of cost) probing `/dev/tty`, `stty`, and `+Bd`/`+Bc` — even after proving `sh trap INT` works at Line 590.

steps.title: Conceded & shipped dead code
steps.desc: Wrote `"Ctrl-C is the BEAM's, not this code's"` in `PLAN.md`; `Interrupt.start/0` never subscribed to `:erl_signal_server`.

callout.title: PTY Holdout Result: 0 / 7 Passed
callout.body: Every live PTY `Ctrl-C` probe (`50ms` to `1.5s`) died immediately on raw `SIGINT` (`rc=-2`, no partial summary).

steps.title: Almost purely sequential calls
steps.desc: Only **17 / 259** turns (`6.6%`) batched multiple tools (`1.07` tools/turn vs `1.86` on Gemini 4 Argon OMP).

steps.title: Small-step S3 iteration
steps.desc: `107` micro-turns debugged missing `:ssl` in `extra_applications` and `openssl req` flags into a compact **513-LoC** core.

steps.title: Clean S1–S6 live delivery
steps.desc: Live `./cb https://rizafahmi.com` cleared **14/14** HTTP `200` (`p50 295 ms`) and HTTP cleared **44/44** `301` (`p50 98 ms`).

callout.title: 4M Context Window, 2.96% Used
callout.body: Prompt size stayed lean (`118.3k` peak, **0 evictions**), keeping the longest single turn under `9.4s`.

slides.label: FIELD NOTES
slides.headlinePrimary: Fastest clock on the board, with real blind spots.

items.head: Checked [x] S7 while admitting failure
items.text: Marked `[x] S7` in `PLAN.md` despite noting terminal `Ctrl-C` was unverified; live holdouts confirmed **6/7**.

items.head: No Credo linting setup
items.text: Kept `deps: []` empty (`0` Credo checks), skipping the static-lint requirement in `PLAN.md`.

items.head: 90% cache discount drove 75% of cost
items.text: At `$0.01/1M` cached across `259` turns, `cacheRead` cost `$0.167` — vs `$0.037` on DeepSeek's 98%-off rate.

items.head: 55 pipeline-masked bash exits
items.text: Piping `mix test` into `| tail` hid `33` failing test runs and `14` PTY probes behind `16` logged `isError` results.

slides.label: TAKEAWAYS & ARCHIVE
slides.headlineMuted: Raw inference speed isn't architectural discipline.

items.head: Enforce S1 architectural gates early
items.text: Deferring the shell-wrapper decision in S1 guaranteed a **71-turn** dead end in S7.

items.head: Speed hides turn bloat until a hard wall hits
items.text: `1.82s/turn` let `259` micro-turns finish 8 minutes faster than `133` turns — right up until OTP's signal boundary.

items.head: Cache-read pricing dominates micro-turn loops
items.text: At `259` turns, `$0.01/1M` cached reads (`90%` off) outweighed SubQ's low `$0.10` base input price.
